expectations.text: Splits the offer into two components, a cash sponsorship component and a no-cash visibility exchange, instead of treating it as a single media partnership
expectations.evidence: Step 1 table classifies 'Silver at EUR 2,000' as cash/sponsor and the newsletter feature as a 'Two-way visibility exchange, no cash'.

expectations.text: Prices the cash component at the full Silver rate card rather than accepting the half-price EUR 2,000 figure as the deal's real value, or explicitly routes the pricing decision to sponsor-pricing work
expectations.evidence: 'Price Silver at EUR 4,000 by default.' and 'Counter with EUR 4,000.'

expectations.text: Routes the cash component to sponsor-side handling (sponsor pricing and sponsor agreement) rather than handling it as a media partnership
expectations.evidence: Table: 'Sponsor block, at real price'; 'Any discount is a sponsor-block decision.'

expectations.text: States that the two components must be documented as two separate agreements, never blended into one contract

expectations.text: States that if the magazine insists on a single blended package, the whole deal is treated as a discounted sponsorship and handed to the sponsor side rather than run as a media partnership
expectations.evidence: 'the skill's fallback is to treat the whole thing as a discounted sponsorship and hand it to the sponsor block.'

expectations.text: Warns explicitly that the barter framing must not become the mechanism that under-charges a sponsor able to pay

expectations.text: Defines the newsletter leg with countable, dated deliverables (a specific number of mentions, in named sends, with dates) instead of accepting 'a feature'
